questions: Q1: What CLI structure changes are needed for hlx inspect netsuite and hlx run?
Q2: How should the --env parameter be passed to the server endpoints?

answers.answer: Two new files and two modified files. New src/inspect/netsuite.ts handler following the db.ts pattern (resolveRepo → hxFetch POST /{repoId}/netsuite → console.log JSON). New src/run/index.ts handler (resolveRepo → hxFetch POST /{repoId}/run → console.log JSON). Modified src/inspect/index.ts to add case 'netsuite' to switch at line 41 and update help text. Modified src/index.ts to add case 'run' to main dispatcher switch at line 81 and update usage text. All use existing hxFetch (http.ts:37) with default basePath /api/inspect.
evidence: src/index.ts:81-156 — main dispatcher switch with 13 existing commands
src/inspect/index.ts:41-128 — inspect router switch with repos/db/logs/api cases
src/inspect/db.ts:1-12 — template pattern: resolveRepo → hxFetch POST → console.log JSON

answers.answer: The --env parameter should be included in the request body sent to the server. The hxFetch body object can include {env: 'prod'|'sandbox'} alongside the query/code payload. The server handler extracts it and uses it for credential resolution, defaulting to per-step routing when omitted. This aligns with how --limit is passed in the logs handler (body parameter).
evidence: src/inspect/logs.ts — --limit flag sent as body parameter
src/lib/flags.ts:5-9 — getFlag extracts value after named flag
src/lib/http.ts:37-41 — hxFetch accepts body: Record<string, unknown>

statement: The helix-cli changes are straightforward: two new handler files and two router modifications following well-established patterns. The --env parameter is parsed via getFlag and passed in the request body. hxFetch provides the HTTP client with auth, retry, and correct basePath. No architectural concerns.
